name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean, among the most Republican seats in the country
Crawford's incumbency and roughly 14-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage
Democrat Terri Green's minimal fundraising: about $65,000 raised and $12,000 on hand
Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 96% or better
model.rationale: An R+23 district, a well-funded incumbent seeking another term, and a challenger with almost no money leave virtually no path for an upset; fundamentals and prediction markets alike point to a Republican win by roughly 19 points.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national Democratic wave or an unforeseen scandal involving Crawford could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's First District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points to the right. Rick Crawford has held the seat since 2011 and is running again with the full advantages of incumbency: about $1 million in cash on hand against roughly $12,000 for Democratic nominee Terri Green, who has raised about $65,000. A Libertarian, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Crawford's chances above 95 percent. The national political environment leans modestly toward Democrats this cycle, yet that shift is far smaller than the district's structural Republican advantage. Every available signal points to a Safe Republican hold, with an expected Republican margin near 19 points.
